items.titleEn: Wall Street undecided on gold's near-term trajectory, Main Street flirts with bearish bias after gold hits $4,200/oz ceiling
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices staged a late-week recovery after coming under heavy pressure from hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data, rising Treasury yields, and a firmer dollar, as falling bond yields and reduced expectations for an October Federal Reserve rate hike helped the precious metal recover much of its losses. Spot gold kicked off the week trading at $4,193.59 per ounce on Sunday evening, and the yellow metal briefly climbed above $4,200 as traders continued to monitor the U.S.-Iran conflict and inflation risks from elevated energy prices. The advance quickly faded, however, with gold setting its weekly high at $4,216.91 per ounce on Monday before a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields pushed prices lower through Tuesday’s trading session. The selling accelerated Wednesday after September CPI rose 3.7% annually, exceeding expectations and reinforcing concerns that energy-driven inflation could force the Fed to tighten monetary policy again. Gold broke below $4,100 and set its weekly low at $4,073.35 per ounce at noon on Wednesday, as traders increased bets on an October rate hike and the dollar strengthened.

Gold, silver diverge as Fed-pause expectations collide with rising crude prices - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were near steady and spot silver prices were lower in late U.S. trading Friday, as sharply higher crude oil prices and a modest rebound in Treasury yields offset support from a weaker U.S. dollar and renewed safe-haven demand. Gold failed to sustain its earlier advance toward $4,200 as the technology-led equity selloff intensified and rising energy prices kept inflation concerns in focus. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,167.90 an ounce, down $1.90, or 0.05%, while spot silver was trading near $56.850, down $0.450, or 0.78%. North American equities closed sharply lower, with major technology stocks extending their losses amid concerns about debt-financed artificial intelligence investment and elevated borrowing costs. The S&P 500 fell 84.62 points, or 1.1%, to 7,659.44. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 175.28 points, or 0.3%, to 52,002.41. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 572.99 points, or 2.1%, to 26,140.03, while the Russell 2000 lost 45.90 points, or 1.7%, to 2,721.37. The Nasdaq finished the week down 4.5%, its worst weekly performance since June, as selling in semiconductor, cloud-computing and other AI-related shares accelerated. European equities closed higher, outperforming Wall Street as stronger corporate earnings helped offset concerns about technology valuations and rising financing costs. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.72% to 644.74, completing its strongest weekly advance since late June. Germany's DAX climbed 0.95% to 25,622.61, France's CAC 40 advanced 0.28% to 7,956.70 and the U.K. FTSE 100 rose 0.38% to 10,881.90. Italy's FTSE MIB added 0.93% to 49,857.18. Automobiles, telecommunications and energy stocks led the regional gains, while health care shares underperformed.

items.titleEn: Gold looks to housing, PMI and consumer sentiment data for direction next week
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold heads into the coming week with investors focused on the health of the U.S. economy and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook, as housing, employment and business activity data could drive volatility across precious metals markets. Bullion prices recovered some ground late this week after coming under pressure from stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data, elevated Treasury yields and a firmer dollar. Gold rebounded above $4,150 an ounce Thursday and remained near that level Friday, while silver traded around $57 an ounce. Markets continue to favor a pause at the Fed's October meeting, although persistent inflation pressures have kept expectations for another rate hike before year-end elevated. The coming week's economic calendar is relatively light, but housing data, weekly jobless claims and Friday's PMI and consumer sentiment reports will offer important signals on economic resilience and inflation pressures ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 monetary policy meeting.
